claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! And one more important question:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he does. Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for providing that information.

Just to confirm a few final details:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation, or has he been for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex has been in hospital for a while now. He's been there for a few months, but I still regularly buy things for him - you know, his favorite snacks, books, things like that to make him more comfortable.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. I understand this must be a difficult time for you and Alex.

To assess this properly, I need to know a bit more:

**How many weeks has Alex been in hospital so far?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been there for 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see that Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks, which is longer than the 12-week threshold mentioned in the Child Benefit rules.

However, there is an important exception: you can continue to receive Child Benefit for a child in hospital beyond 12 weeks if you regularly spend money on them, which you've told me you do (buying snacks, books, and other items for Alex).

Before I make my final assessment, let me ask:

**Are there any other circumstances I should know about, such as: Is Alex in a hospital in the UK? And are you and Alex both UK residents (aside from his hospital stay)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in a hospital here in the UK. And yes, we're both UK residents - he's just in hospital for treatment, but this is where we live.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming those details. I now have all the information I need to make an assessment of your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex normally lives with you and you're responsible for him
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex has been in a UK hospital for 15 weeks
- You regularly spend money on him while he's in hospital

The key point here is that while there is normally a 12-week limit for children in hospital, there is an exception: you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on your child while they're in hospital, which you do.

Let me provide you with my final assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Even though Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks (which is longer than the normal 12-week limit), you qualify for an important exception. Because you regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital - buying him snacks, books, and other items - you can continue to receive Child Benefit.

You meet all the other eligibility criteria as well:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You live in the UK and Alex normally lives with you
- You're responsible for Alex
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

I hope Alex recovers well. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit, please feel free to ask!
